chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Leaving Decca for Columbia after comparing studio sound
summary: The Decca studio sound bothered him, so he made V-discs at Columbia and RCA before choosing Columbia on sound alone.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: first arrangements for our band were done on Decca. But -- and I really wasn't as -- I didn't think it was so terribly important. My contract was finally coming to a close, but I didn't think it was all that important to leave Decca, except for one thing: The sound of the Decca studios used to drive me crazy. It never had the same kind of thing that Columbia and Victor had.

Whether it was a question of engineering or what, I don't know. But I do know it was inferior to my ears. And so what I did before I made up my mind where we were going to go, because we had offers from both the other labels, was to do V-discs in Columbia, in the church downtown. And also at the RCA main studios, and then I decided I liked the Columbia sound the best and that's why we wound up going to Columbia. For no other reason.
I wonder how many people would do that today?
I don't think it would happen in circumstances today. That's right, you did a number of things in World War II V-discs. I see them even reappearing today on -- as collectors' items reissues.
I saw some in Sacramento about two or three weeks ago. You were beaming your music overseas, too,
